papers.title: Laser-assisted 3D bioprinting of exocrine pancreas spheroid models for cancer initiation study.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is the most common malignancy of the pancreas. It has shown a poor prognosis and a rising incidence in the developed world. Other pathologies associated with this tissue include pancreatitis, a risk condition for pancreatic cancer. The onset of both pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer follows a common pattern: exocrine pancreatic acinar cells undergo a transdifferentiation to duct cells that triggers a 3D restructuration of the pancreatic tissue. However, the exact mechanism underlying this process remains partially undefined. Further understanding the cellular events leading to PDAC could open new avenues in the development of novel therapeutic approaches. Since current 2D cell culture models fail to mimic the tridimensional complexity of the pancreatic tissue, new in vitro models are urgently needed. Here, we generated 3D pancreatic cell spheroid arrays using laser-assisted bioprinting and characterized their phenotypic evolution over time through image analysis and phenotypic characterization. We show that these bioprinted spheroids, composed of both acinar and ductal cells, can replicate the initial stages of PDAC development. This bioprinted miniaturized spheroid-based array model should prove useful for the study of the internal and external factors that contribute to the formation of precursor PDAC lesions and to cancer progression, and may therefore shed light on future PDAC therapy strategies.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及任何人工智能方法，仅使用激光辅助生物打印构建胰腺球体模型，与AI驱动生物打印的研究方向无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage, lacks experimental validation of an AI model, and does not advance toward autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 构建体外胰腺癌起始模型，研究腺泡细胞转分化机制。
summary_zh.method: 激光辅助生物打印共培养腺泡和导管细胞形成3D球体。
summary_zh.result: 打印球体可模拟胰腺导管腺癌早期发育阶段。
summary_zh.validation: 通过图像分析和表型表征验证球体演化。

summary_en.motivation: To develop an in vitro model of pancreatic cancer initiation by replicating the transdifferentiation of acinar cells using 3D bioprinted spheroids.
summary_en.method: Laser-assisted bioprinting was used to create spheroid arrays composed of both acinar and ductal pancreatic cells.
summary_en.result: The bioprinted spheroids recapitulated early stages of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma development.
summary_en.validation: Phenotypic evolution was characterized via image analysis and phenotypic markers.

papers.title: The metaphyseal sleeve: an unexplored option in the treatment of complex primary knee osteoarthritis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In an ever-aging society that as a whole has become more affluent, significant emphasis has been accorded to an improved quality of life. Knee osteoarthritis is ever-increasingly treated with total knee arthroplasty. The benefits and satisfaction experienced by those who have undergone total knee replacements (TKR) are well documented in the literature. The issue arises when osteoarthritis of the affected knee is more complex than simple osteoarthritis, i.e. the patient has complex primary osteoarthritis. This collective term encompasses conditions such as massive bone loss, ligamentous laxity, coronal defects and those with contractures. There are various classifications to describe massive bone loss but we utilized the Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) classification. Numerous treatment options are available and we report the use of metaphyseal sleeves as a highly successful treatment option. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all the patients at our centre who underwent primary TKR using the metaphyseal sleeves. Patients were assessed on symptoms and functional status, and radiographs were also taken to assess for osseointegration. Only patients who completed 2 years of follow up were included in our study. RESULTS: The updated (2011) Knee Society Score (KSS) was used in conjunction with radiological assessments at each follow up. Mean KSS scores improved from 53.83 preoperatively to 193.39 postoperatively. All patients demonstrated increasing osseointegration throughout follow up. CONCLUSION: The metaphyseal sleeve is an excellent treatment option for complex primary osteoarthritic knees with good results objectively, functionally and radiologically and would be a great choice for all orthopaedic surgeons to include in their armamentarium.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为回顾性临床研究，评估骨水泥套筒在复杂膝关节置换中的效果，不涉及任何增材制造或生物力学测试。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical retrospective review of metaphyseal sleeves in knee replacement, with no LPBF fabrication, no mechanical testing, no porous structure optimization, no fatigue analysis, and no surface roughness characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估骨水泥套筒在复杂原发性膝骨关节炎治疗中的效果。

summary_zh.validation: 临床随访结合影像学评估。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the clinical outcomes of metaphyseal sleeves in complex primary total knee arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A retrospective review of patients who underwent primary TKR with metaphyseal sleeves, with minimum 2-year follow-up.
summary_en.result: Mean Knee Society Scores improved significantly and all patients showed progressive osseointegration.
summary_en.validation: Clinical and radiographic assessments at follow-up visits.
